owner_steps: The owner has the device in hand, unlocked, trusted and charged; the automation build is installed by the campaign (signing is the owner's).
The owner turns gears by dragging around them, drags and taps the lamp, double-taps gears and orbits with two fingers; the campaign does not synthesise touches on hardware.
rows.pass: Touch-to-frame latency recorded for 200 samples per device; a drag around a gear while playing turns the train one tooth per 360° ÷ T swept (T the gear's teeth) the way the finger went and sends that many handle turns on release; a vertical drag on the lamp or its ladder steps it one rung per 24 points; a tap on the lamp while playing sends exactly one run; a second tap on a gear other than the driver within 0.35 s and 22 points re-seats it once; a double tap on empty space restores the authored camera.
rows.procedure: Drag around a gear to turn the train, drag the lamp up and down, tap the lamp to run, double-tap a gear to re-seat it, orbit the camera with two fingers and double-tap empty space on each device; the campaign records the interval from touch to the first frame showing the change.
rows.title: Touch feel and touch-to-frame latency

rows.procedure: Turn the Sound toggle on and play a level to a win and to a failure with the haptics switch on, including one refused action (re-seating the driver, which the rules refuse); choose a gear to hear its audition; observe the clockwork's ambient sound and the selection, success, warning and error haptics.
